issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig races and breaks under concurrent requests
issues.detail: The TritonLoraConfig instance is shared across all requests for a LoRA. Two concurrent first-time requests both see is_registered=False, both load .npy files, and one may set is_registered=True before the other has actually transmitted weights to the backend. The invariant 'is_registered==True iff backend has cached this task_id' is not maintained under concurrency. Needs a lock or per-request weight inclusion until an ack.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is non-deterministic and not unique across model repositories
issues.detail: task_id starts at 1 and increments per LoRA per call to _parse_lora_configs, but it is called per base model. Two base models sharing the TRT-LLM backend will collide on task_ids 1, 2, 3..., causing the backend's LoRA cache to serve the wrong adapter. The invariant 'task_id uniquely identifies a (weights, config) tuple in the backend cache' does not hold. Needs a global counter or a hash of the path.

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production hot paths
issues.detail: `print(f"backend: {backend}")` fires inside the per-LoRA loop on every metadata refresh, and `print(traceback.format_exc())` was added to three FastAPI routers plus the parse function. These belong behind a logger at DEBUG level. The asymptotic cost is small but the practical noise on a busy server is not — and silent swallow-then-print of tracebacks defeats structured logging.

issues.description: Synchronous np.load on every cold LoRA request blocks the async event loop
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request is invoked from async chat/completion handlers, but np.load on .lora_weights.npy and .lora_config.npy is synchronous file I/O plus deserialization. For multi-MB adapters this can stall the event loop for tens of ms. The fix is to pre-load weights at parse time into the TritonLoraConfig, trading memory for predictable latency, or to offload via run_in_executor.

issues.description: Return type annotation lies about the actual return type
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs is annotated `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but returns `List[TritonLoraConfig]` or None. This is a stale annotation from the rename. A reader trying to follow the code without running it is actively misled — exactly the readability failure literate programming exists to prevent.

issues.description: _get_lora_config return annotation says TritonLoraConfig but it returns None on the common path
issues.detail: The signature `-> TritonLoraConfig` is wrong; the function returns None when lora_name is None or lora_configs is None. Should be `Optional[TritonLoraConfig]`. Also, model_metadata.get(model_name) can return None, after which `.lora_configs` will raise AttributeError rather than a clean ClientError — the invariant 'caller already validated model_name exists' is not stated.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The feature lands the right shape but its two load-bearing invariants — "task_id uniquely identifies a cached adapter" and "is_registered reflects backend cache state" — do not survive a concurrency or multi-model audit. Both are P0 correctness risks the test plan would not catch without adversarial load. Several smaller literate-programming failures (lying type annotations, stray debug prints, sync I/O on the async path) compound the readability cost. The algorithmic core is fine; the rigor around shared mutable state and identifier allocation needs another pass before this is safe to ship.
